record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.original_question: Given n jobs to be processed on a single machine, where job j has linearly deteriorating time-dependent processing time p_j(t) = 1 + b_j t when it starts at time t, and where C_j is the completion time of job j in a schedule, determine the computational complexity of finding a schedule that minimizes the total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this problem polynomial-time solvable, or can it be proved NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem. There are $n$ jobs $1,2,\dots,n$ to be processed without preemption on a single machine, which can process at most one job at a time and is continuously available from time $0$. Each job $j$ has an associated nonnegative real deterioration rate $b_j \ge 0$. If job $j$ starts being processed at time $t \ge 0$, then its processing time is the time-dependent (linearly deteriorating) value
$$p_j(t) = 1 + b_j t.$$
A schedule is a permutation $\pi = (\pi(1),\dots,\pi(n))$ of the jobs; processing starts at time $0$, and each job begins as soon as the preceding job finishes. Let $C_j(\pi)$ denote the completion time of job $j$ under schedule $\pi$. The objective is to minimize the total completion time
$$\sum_{j=1}^{n} C_j(\pi)$$
over all permutations $\pi$.

Determine the computational complexity of this optimization problem. In particular, decide whether it can be solved in polynomial time in $n$ (and the bit-length of the inputs $b_j$), or whether it is NP-hard, at least in the ordinary (weak) sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of minimizing total completion time on a single machine with linearly deteriorating processing times of the form $p_j = 1 + b_j t$ (unit basic processing times) is widely reported as still open. A 2020 paper in the Journal of Scheduling by Gawiejnowicz and collaborators is explicitly devoted to "new results for an open time-dependent scheduling problem" of this exact form, providing only structural properties (e.g., sharper necessary optimality conditions reducing the cardinality of the set of candidate optimal schedules), but not resolving its polynomial-time solvability or NP-hardness. No subsequent resolution was found in the search.
